主要内容: SanDisk Corporation released its financial results for the fourth quarter and fiscal year ended January 3, 2016. The report included both GAAP and non-GAAP financial measures, with the latter excluding certain expenses, gains, and losses to provide a clearer view of core operating performance. The non-GAAP results were highlighted as useful for both management and investors, as they align with financial models used by analysts. The report also mentioned the exclusion of expenses related to share-based compensation and amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets from acquisitions such as Pliant Technology, Inc. and FlashSoft Corporation. The text discusses the financial reporting practices of Information Technology, Inc., including the use of non-GAAP financial measures. It mentions several acquisitions, such as SMART Storage Systems in August 2013 and Fusion-io, Inc. in July 2014. The text also references Western Digital Corporation and its acquisition-related expenses. The company explains that non-GAAP measures are used to assess performance, allocate resources, and plan for the future. These measures exclude certain charges like share-based compensation, amortization of intangible assets, and inventory step-up expenses. The text emphasizes that non-GAAP results should be used in conjunction with GAAP results and not as a substitute. The information provided is part of an 8-K filing dated January 27, 2016. The 8-K filing from SanDisk outlines forward-looking statements regarding the proposed merger with Western Digital’s subsidiary, Schrader Acquisition Corporation. These statements include anticipated benefits and the expected closing date of the merger. The filing highlights various risks associated with the merger, such as the inability to obtain stockholder approval, regulatory hurdles, integration challenges, and potential disruptions to business operations. The risks are further detailed in the preliminary joint proxy statement/prospectus filed with the SEC. The merger is subject to numerous uncertainties, including the timing of the transaction and the ability of both companies to retain key personnel. The filing serves as a disclosure of potential risks and uncertainties related to the proposed merger. This 8-K filing from SanDisk and Western Digital outlines the proposed merger between the two companies. The document includes a preliminary joint proxy statement/prospectus, which is part of a Registration Statement on Form S-4 filed with the SEC. The filing was amended on January 27, 2016, and both companies plan to file additional documents with the SEC regarding the merger. Investors are urged to read the joint proxy statement/prospectus and other relevant documents carefully as they contain important information about the proposed merger. The documents can be accessed on the SEC’s website and the respective company websites. The filing highlights the regulatory and legal aspects of the merger, including the need for shareholder approval and the potential risks involved.
